newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Profitability of Brazil banks seen modestly lower.
newsitem.headline: Profitability of Brazil banks seen modestly lower.

text.p: Profitability of Brazil's banks is likely to recede in the second half, as the sector can no longer count on falling loan defaults, higher service revenues and subsidiary gains to boost earnings, a consultant said on Tuesday.

"It appears that banks already have profited what they could from lower defaults, banking service revenues and gains from subsidiaries," said Erivelto Rodrigues, director at Austin Asis banking consulting firm.
"The banks' big challenge now is to increase assets, that means to boost credit operations and expand their client base," he said.

Banks in the first half showed a record medium annualized return on equity of 16.5 percent, up from 12.4 percent in the same period last year, according to an Austin Asis survey on the first-half results of 61 private and state-owned banks.
The survey includes Brazil's top retail banks such as Bradesco, Banco Itau, Unibanco and Banco Real.
Rodrigues said most of the banks in the first six months of the year benefited from cuts in expenses related to loan loss provisions as defaults fell sharply.
"The loan defaults ratio in the banking system improved significantly in the first half," he said.

Still, Rodrigues said a rise in corporate and consumer defaults in July, evidenced in the most recent data from the Sao Paulo Commerce Association (ACSP), may have an impact on the banking sector by the end of the year.
